answer: Trust comes from a lottery jury. First, a newcomer stakes 200 tokens on a claim, a public signal. Second, a random beacon draws five jurors from five districts, so attackers cannot pick judges or echo their own votes. Third, jurors re-run the work; all five must agree, and a false pass costs each 500 tokens. Fourth, twenty claims in sixty days unlock full trading, and no agent may wander to game the draw. Forging 10,000 fakes needs 200,000 claims and 1M juror-hours, over $8 million. Like a signal trusted only when five keepers agree, trust is granted by strangers, never bought.
